title: I Paid for Every Meal Kit So You Don't Have To
creator: Marcus Bell
description:
Four meal kits, four weeks, one small apartment kitchen and way too much cardboard.

The boxes I tried: HelloFresh, Blue Apron, Home Chef, Factor. Prices are what I paid in September in Chicago and will be different where you are.

sentences.t: So for the last month, every single dinner I've cooked has come out of a cardboard box.
Four weeks, four different meal kits, and I want to figure out which one is actually worth the money.
My recycling bin is full, my neighbors think I'm running a warehouse, let's go.
Week one was HelloFresh, and I'll start with the boring practical stuff.
Three meals for two people came out to about seventy dollars after shipping, so roughly twelve bucks a plate.
Ingredients were fine, the produce was a little sad, there was a lime that had seen things.
Best meal was a chicken shawarma bowl, worst was a pasta that tasted like the idea of pasta.
Now, I need to stop for a second, because some of you are going to be suspicious, and that's fair.
HelloFresh has sponsored a couple of my videos before, and Factor reached out last year about a deal that I said no to.
This video is not one of those, nobody is paying for it, and none of these companies know it exists.
I ordered every box on my own card at full price, no influencer codes, no free boxes in the mail.
If anything in this video sounds like an ad, it's just because I liked the food, I promise.
Okay, week two, Blue Apron.
Blue Apron has always felt like the fancy one, and the recipes are definitely more involved.
One night took me fifty five minutes when the card said thirty, and I'm not a slow cook.
But the food was genuinely good, there was a seared salmon with a brown butter thing that I would make again on my own.
The packaging, though, every single ingredient in its own little plastic bag, I counted twenty three bags in one box.
Week three was Home Chef, and this one surprised me.
They have these oven ready meals where everything comes in a tray and you just put it in the oven.
Is that cooking?
Not really, but on a Tuesday when I got home at eight, I did not care at all.
Taste was solid, portions were the biggest of the four, and it came out cheapest per plate too.
Week four was Factor, which isn't really a meal kit, it's fully made meals you microwave.
Two minutes in the microwave, done, and honestly it was better than I expected from a microwave meal.
But it also felt like I was eating airline food at home, every day, alone, at my counter.
By Thursday I missed chopping an onion, which is a sentence I never thought I'd say.
Alright, rankings.
For actually learning to cook and food that tastes great, Blue Apron, if you can handle the plastic and the time.
For busy weeks and best value, Home Chef, and it's not especially close.
HelloFresh sits right in the middle, it's fine at everything and great at nothing.
And Factor I'd only use if I was truly drowning, like a newborn baby or exam season level drowning.
Honestly though, the real winner was my grocery store, because when I went back this week I spent forty bucks on six dinners.
Let me know which one you'd pick, and if you've got a meal kit horror story, the comments are yours.
